english_meaning: Able to last a long time without breaking or wearing out.
gujarati_meaning: ઘણા સમય સ્‌ ​udhee toot ya vankhi utarya vina tikuvu ble.
usage_note: 'Durable goods' are long-lasting products like appliances and furniture.
examples: This bag is made from durable leather.
Durable products save money in the long run.
She chose the durable option for outdoor use.
The jacket is stylish and durable.

english_meaning: Truly what it is claimed to be; not fake or counterfeit.
gujarati_meaning: jo kehvay che te j sachi rite che; nakli ya duplicate nahi.
usage_note: 'Genuine article' means the real thing. Used often in quality assurance.
examples: This is a genuine leather handbag.
The certificate proves the painting is genuine.
She only buys genuine products.
Be careful of fake goods sold as genuine.

english_meaning: Made in imitation of something genuine, with intent to deceive.
gujarati_meaning: thaganat karvani niyat-thi asli vastunu nakli-blo-tiyar karelu.
usage_note: Selling counterfeit goods is illegal and can result in criminal charges.
memory_tip: 'Counter' = against + 'feit' = ble (Old French) → counterfeit = asli-ni-saamnu nakli.
examples: The market was full of counterfeit watches.
Police seized counterfeit currency notes.
Buying counterfeit goods supports illegal trade.
The bag was a counterfeit of a luxury brand.

english_meaning: A written guarantee from a manufacturer to repair or replace a defective product within a set time.
gujarati_meaning: nirmat-a taraf-thi lakhit hemti ke nakkhi samay-ma khami hou to saadhse ya badlavse.
usage_note: Warranty covers manufacturing defects; 'guarantee' is often used interchangeably.
memory_tip: 'Warrant' = ble adhikaar → warranty = ble saadhva-nu adhikaar.
examples: This TV comes with a 2-year warranty.
The laptop is still under warranty.
She claimed a warranty replacement for the faulty phone.
Always keep your warranty card safe.

english_meaning: Having a fault or flaw; not working properly.
gujarati_meaning: ble khami ya toot hoy; sari rite kam na kare.
usage_note: You are entitled to a refund or replacement for defective products.
memory_tip: 'De' = without + 'fect' = ble kari shaku → defective = ble kari shakva-nu nathi (flaw).
examples: The fan was defective and stopped working.
She returned the defective item for a refund.
A defective batch was recalled by the company.
Defective products damage a brand's reputation.

gujarati_meaning: bilkul navu ane upyog na thayelu.
usage_note: 'Brand new' emphasises the product has never been used before.
memory_tip: 'Brand' = ble stamp + 'new' = navu → brand new = ble stamp karelu navu (fresh from factory).
examples: She bought a brand new laptop for college.
The car is brand new — never driven.
Brand new items come in original packaging.
I prefer buying brand new over second-hand.

english_meaning: Previously owned or used by someone else.
gujarati_meaning: pahela ble bija koi-ae upyog karelu ya ma-likhi hoy.
usage_note: Also called 'pre-owned' especially for cars. Thrift stores sell second-hand goods.
memory_tip: 'Second' = bijo + 'hand' = haath → second-hand = be-o no haath lagyu chhe.
examples: She bought a second-hand bicycle at low cost.
Second-hand books are much cheaper.
The second-hand market is growing online.
He sold his second-hand phone for ₹5,000.

english_meaning: Of superior quality and usually higher price; also an additional payment.
gujarati_meaning: uchhi quality ane saamanye ble mota bhav; ya ble vadhanu bhetru.
usage_note: Premium products justify higher prices with better quality or features.
examples: This is a premium brand of coffee.
She paid a premium for the limited edition watch.
Premium seats offer extra legroom on the flight.
Premium quality materials last longer.

english_meaning: Low-cost; also a plan for managing income and expenses.
gujarati_meaning: ble ble ochha kharch; ya aavak ane kharcha manage karava-nu ble aayojan.
usage_note: 'On a budget' means managing with limited money.
memory_tip: 'Budget' = ble ble ankhe-bal ble (purse in Old French) → budget = ble purse manage.
examples: She found a budget hotel for the trip.
We planned a holiday on a tight budget.
Budget smartphones are great for students.
He set a monthly budget for shopping.

english_meaning: Not harmful to the environment; designed to have a minimal ecological impact.
gujarati_meaning: paryavaran-ne nukshan-karak na hoy; ble-nana paryavaran prabhav-thi ble-banavel.
usage_note: Look for eco-friendly certifications like 'recyclable' or 'biodegradable' on packaging.
examples: She prefers eco-friendly cleaning products.
The brand uses eco-friendly packaging.
Eco-friendly cars produce fewer emissions.
Buying eco-friendly products helps the planet.

gujarati_meaning: saheli-thi tootay, nuksan-paame, ya nasht thaay.
usage_note: Fragile stickers are placed on packages to warn handlers to be careful.
examples: This vase is very fragile — handle with care.
The parcel was marked 'Fragile'.
Fragile items should be wrapped in bubble wrap.
She carefully packed the fragile glassware.

english_meaning: Able to be used in many different ways or for many different purposes.
gujarati_meaning: ble ghano upyogi — ble ghani rite ya ghani jagya upayog thay.
usage_note: Versatile products offer more value as they serve multiple functions.
memory_tip: 'Verse' = ble pharvatu → versatile = ble ghani-rite pharvatu (multi-use).
examples: This knife is versatile — it cuts vegetables and meat.
She bought a versatile dress for multiple occasions.
A versatile bag works for work and travel.
Versatile tools are popular in hardware stores.

english_meaning: Closely and neatly packed together; small and practical.
gujarati_meaning: ble nankanku ane vyavhari; ghanamaan khodayelu.
usage_note: Compact products are preferred for travel or small living spaces.
memory_tip: 'Com' + 'pact' = sathe + dabayelu → compact = ble dabayu jema ghanu smaay.
examples: She chose a compact camera for her travels.
The compact car is easy to park in the city.
The apartment has a compact but efficient kitchen.
Compact laptops are popular among students.

english_meaning: Unable to be penetrated or damaged by water.
gujarati_meaning: jema pani ble ghusi na shake ya nuksan na kare.
usage_note: Waterproof = fully protected from water. Water-resistant = partially protected.
memory_tip: 'Water' = pani + 'proof' = sabit → waterproof = pani thi sabit/surakhsit.
examples: She bought a waterproof jacket for the monsoon.
This phone is waterproof up to 30 metres.
Waterproof boots are essential for hiking.
The tent is waterproof and lightweight.

english_meaning: Made by hand rather than by machine; often implying higher quality or craftsmanship.
gujarati_meaning: machine ne badle haath-thi banavelhu; ghani vaakht uchhi quality ya kaarigiri-nu suchak.
usage_note: Handmade products are often more expensive due to the craftsmanship involved.
examples: She sells handmade jewellery at the craft fair.
The handmade pottery was unique and beautiful.
Handmade chocolates make a perfect gift.
Handmade products often cost more than factory-made.

english_meaning: A product produced in a small, specific quantity, often making it more exclusive and valuable.
gujarati_meaning: ble maryadit sankhyama banavelhu ble utpad, ble ghani vaakht ble exclusive ane kimti banave.
usage_note: Limited edition products create urgency and exclusivity among buyers.
memory_tip: 'Limited' = maryadit + 'edition' = aavrutti → limited edition = maryadit avrutti (sirf kuch j!).
examples: She bought a limited edition perfume.
The limited edition sneakers sold out in minutes.
Collectors pay high prices for limited edition items.
The brand released a limited edition for Diwali.
